lessons.title: 11.7 Right Triangle Trigonometry
lessons.html:
📖 Right Triangle Trigonometry
SOH-CAH-TOA, and the ratio you need is decided by which sides you have.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

Right Triangle Trigonometry

Use of side ratios to connect angles and lengths in right triangles.

dimension

A measurable length, width, height, or radius.

theorem

A mathematical statement proved to be true.

diagram

A labeled drawing representing geometric information.

In a right triangle, sinθ = opposite/hypotenuse, cosθ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tanθ = opposite/adjacent. Label the sides relative to the angle you are using, not to the page.

The SAT also tests the complementary relationship: sinθ = cos(90° − θ). That identity appears as a question in its own right.

Key points

  • SOH-CAH-TOA — sine, cosine and tangent as side ratios.
  • Label opposite and adjacent relative to the angle in question.
  • sinθ = cos(90° − θ) for complementary angles.
  • Use the ratio matching the two sides you have or want.
  • Special triangles give exact values: sin30° = 1/2, sin45° = √2/2, sin60° = √3/2.
  • Trigonometric ratios apply to right triangles only.

Example

A right triangle has an opposite side of 3 and a hypotenuse of 5. sinθ = 3/5. The adjacent side is 4 (a 3-4-5 triple), so cosθ = 4/5 and tanθ = 3/4.

Why this matters

Trigonometry is a small but reliable part of the Geometry and Trigonometry domain, and the complementary-angle identity is tested more often than any computation.

lessons.title: 12.1 Time Management
lessons.html:
📖 Time Management
The clock is the same for everyone; pacing is what differs.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

pacing

The controlled speed used to complete a timed section.

checkpoint

A planned time for comparing progress with minutes remaining.

time trap

A question consuming excessive time relative to its value.

review window

Reserved time for checking uncertain answers.

Reading & Writing gives 27 questions in 32 minutes, roughly 70 seconds each. Math gives 22 questions in 35 minutes, roughly 95 seconds each. Questions within a module are broadly ordered by difficulty in Math and grouped by type in Reading & Writing.

The single most valuable habit is abandoning a question you are stuck on. Flag it, move on, and return. Two easy questions later in the module are worth more than one hard one you are determined to finish.

Key points

  • Reading & Writing: about 70 seconds per question.
  • Math: about 95 seconds per question.
  • Flag and move on after roughly double your target time.
  • Every question is worth the same mark, whatever its difficulty.
  • Reach the end of the module — unseen questions score nothing.
  • Leave two minutes to answer everything still blank.

Example

A student spends four minutes on question 9 of Math and never reaches questions 20–22. He got question 9 right. He lost three marks to gain one, and two of those three were easier than the one he solved.

Why this matters

Pacing costs nothing to learn and is worth more marks than most content revision, because unanswered questions are guaranteed zeros while guesses are not.

lessons.title: 12.2 Adaptive Testing Strategy
lessons.html:
📖 Adaptive Testing Strategy
Module 1 sets your ceiling, so spend your best effort there.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

adaptive testing

A system that selects a later module partly from earlier performance.

routing

The process used to assign the second module.

difficulty

The level of reasoning or complexity required by an item.

accuracy

The proportion of questions answered correctly.

Each section's module 1 is routed: perform well and module 2 comes from the harder pool, which is scaled to reach the top of the 200–800 range. Perform poorly and module 2 is easier, with a lower ceiling.

The practical consequence is counterintuitive. Conventional advice says spread your effort evenly. On the Digital SAT, module 1 accuracy matters more than module 2 accuracy, so never rush module 1 to bank time.

Key points

  • Module 1 routes you to the easier or harder module 2.
  • Only the harder module 2 reaches the upper score range.
  • Never rush module 1 to save time — there is no time carried over.
  • The sections adapt independently of each other.
  • If module 2 feels hard, that is usually a good sign.
  • Accuracy in module 1 beats speed in module 1.

Example

Two students each answer 30 of 54 Reading & Writing questions correctly. The one who concentrated her accuracy in module 1 was routed to the harder module 2 and scored higher. Identical totals, different scores.

Why this matters

This is the single strategic difference between the Digital SAT and every paper test before it, and most preparation material written before 2023 gets it wrong.

lessons.title: 12.3 Guessing Techniques
lessons.html:
📖 Guessing Techniques
No penalty for a wrong answer means never leaving a blank.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

educated guess

A choice made using reasoning when the answer is uncertain.

estimation

Finding an approximate value to judge plausibility.

distractor

A plausible but incorrect option.

probability

The likelihood that a choice is correct.

The SAT subtracts nothing for an incorrect response. A blank scores zero with certainty; a guess among four options scores 25% of the time, and better than that after eliminating even one choice.

Eliminate before guessing. Removing one option raises your odds to one in three, and two to one in two. On student-produced response questions, enter a plausible value rather than nothing.

Key points

  • There is no penalty for a wrong answer — never leave a blank.
  • Blind guessing among four is 25%; after one elimination, 33%; after two, 50%.
  • Use the Bluebook option eliminator to cross out as you reason.
  • Extreme or absolute wording is usually eliminable in Reading & Writing.
  • In Math, discard answers of implausible magnitude or the wrong sign.
  • For student-produced responses, type a reasonable value rather than leaving it empty.

Example

With two minutes left and three questions unanswered, filling all three blindly is worth about 0.75 marks on average. Leaving them is worth exactly zero. It costs ten seconds.

Why this matters

This is the cheapest advice on the test and the most frequently ignored. Candidates trained on penalty-scored exams still leave blanks out of habit.

lessons.title: 12.4 Eliminating Wrong Answers
lessons.html:
📖 Eliminating Wrong Answers
Finding three wrong answers is often easier than finding one right one.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

elimination

Systematic removal of answer choices that cannot be correct.

contradiction

A statement incompatible with given information.

scope shift

An answer becoming broader or narrower than the source.

irrelevance

Lack of a direct connection to the question.

Every multiple-choice question has three distractors, and they are constructed rather than random. Learning what they look like lets you remove them quickly and confidently.

In Reading & Writing, distractors are typically too extreme, outside the passage, or true-but-irrelevant. In Math, they are the result of a predictable error — a sign flip, a missed step, or answering the wrong question.

Key points

  • Reading & Writing distractors: too extreme, not in the passage, true but off-point.
  • Math distractors: sign errors, half-finished work, the other variable's value.
  • Use the Bluebook option eliminator so ruled-out choices stay ruled out.
  • If two choices say the same thing differently, neither is usually right.
  • In Math, check magnitude and sign before doing any arithmetic.
  • Elimination plus a guess beats a blank every time.

Example

A question asks for y after solving a system. The value of x is almost always among the choices, because the test knows some candidates will stop a step early. Checking what was asked eliminates it instantly.

Why this matters

Elimination is a general-purpose tool that works when your method fails, which is exactly when you need it most.

lessons.title: 12.5 Common Mistakes
lessons.html:
📖 Common Mistakes
Most lost marks come from a short list of avoidable habits.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

error analysis

Study of why a mistake occurred and how to prevent it.

misread

Incorrect understanding of a prompt or condition.

careless error

A preventable mistake despite knowing the method.

correction plan

A specific action for eliminating a repeated problem.

Scores are rarely lost to material a candidate never learned. They are lost to answering the wrong question, mis-copying a number, flipping a sign, leaving blanks, and spending four minutes on one item.

The remedy is a checking habit rather than more content revision: before submitting an answer, confirm it answers what was asked and is plausible.

Key points

  • Answering the wrong question — x when y was asked, or the change when the total was.
  • Sign errors, especially when distributing a minus across brackets.
  • Misreading units, or radius given as diameter.
  • Leaving blanks despite there being no penalty.
  • Over-investing in one hard question and not reaching later easy ones.
  • Ignoring the qualifiers not, except and least in a question stem.

Example

A student solves a percent question correctly and reports the new price when the question asked for the increase. Full method, correct arithmetic, no mark. The error was in the last two seconds.

Why this matters

Reviewing an error log by reason rather than by topic usually reveals that two or three habits account for most lost marks — and habits are faster to fix than knowledge gaps.

lessons.title: 12.6 Stress Management
lessons.html:
📖 Stress Management
A calm candidate reads the question correctly; that is most of the benefit.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

test anxiety

Worry or physical tension associated with an assessment.

controlled breathing

Deliberate breath regulation used to reduce arousal.

grounding

Directing attention to immediate sensory experience.

reframing

Replacing an unhelpful thought with a useful interpretation.

Test anxiety costs marks through mechanical errors: misreading stems, rushing, and abandoning a method halfway. Preparation reduces it more than any technique, because familiarity removes surprise.

In the room, a slow breath and a deliberate re-read of the question is usually enough to recover. If a module has gone badly, put it down: the next module is scored on its own.

Key points

  • Full timed practice reduces anxiety more than any relaxation technique.
  • Slow breathing steadies attention: in for four, out for six.
  • Re-read the stem when you feel rushed — misreading is the main cost of panic.
  • Do not carry a bad module into the next one; they are scored separately.
  • Sleep normally for several nights, not just the night before.
  • Avoid last-minute cramming on the morning of the test.

Example

A candidate blanks on a Math question, breathes slowly, re-reads, and notices the question gave a diameter where she had used it as a radius. Thirty seconds of calm recovered a mark she had already lost.

Why this matters

Anxiety is not a character problem; it is a preparation and technique problem, and both respond to practice under realistic conditions.

lessons.title: 12.7 Test-Day Checklist
lessons.html:
📖 Test-Day Checklist
Everything that can be settled the night before, settle the night before.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

checklist

A written list used to verify every required preparation.

valid ID

An accepted document confirming a test taker's identity.

admission information

Registration details needed for check-in.

contingency plan

A prepared response to a possible device or travel problem.

The morning of the test is the worst possible time to discover a flat battery, a missing admission ticket or a name mismatch on your ID. Assemble everything the evening before and leave it by the door.

Complete Bluebook exam setup days ahead, not on the morning. Charge your device fully and bring the charger anyway.

Key points

  • Passport matching your registration, plus the admission ticket.
  • Device fully charged, Bluebook installed, exam setup already completed.
  • Charger, and an approved calculator if you prefer your own to Desmos.
  • Phone and smart watch off and stored — through the break too.
  • Arrive at least 30 minutes early; latecomers are not admitted.
  • Eat beforehand; the test runs over two hours with one short break.

Example

The night before: passport, ticket, charged laptop, charger and water by the door. Bluebook setup done three days earlier. Alarm set for a departure 30 minutes earlier than strictly necessary. Nothing left to decide in the morning.

Why this matters

None of this improves your English or your maths. All of it protects the score those months of work have already earned.

questions.question: Rice and beans are planted 3 : 5 across 64 hectares. How much is rice?
questions.explanation: There are 8 shares; one share is 8 hectares, so rice occupies 3 × 8 = 24 hectares.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x², what is f(g(3))?
questions.explanation: Work inside out: g(3) = 9, then f(9) = 2(9) + 1 = 19.

questions.question: Simplify (x² − 9)/(x − 3).
questions.explanation: Factoring the numerator as (x − 3)(x + 3) allows the common factor to cancel, leaving x + 3.

questions.question: For the values 20, 22, 24, 26, 400, which is true?
options: The mean best represents the data
The median is 24 and better represents the data
The mean and median are equal
questions.explanation: The extreme value pulls the mean to 98.4 while the median stays at 24, describing the data better.

questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon measures:
questions.explanation: The interior sum is (6 − 2) × 180 = 720°, and dividing by 6 gives 120°.

questions.question: In a Math system question asking for y, why does the value of x usually appear as a choice?
options: Because candidates who stop a step early will select it
questions.explanation: Distractors are built from predictable errors, including answering the wrong part of the question.

questions.question: When does the Digital SAT adapt to your performance?
options: Between module 1 and module 2 of a section
questions.explanation: The Digital SAT is multistage adaptive: module 1 performance routes you into an easier or harder module 2.

questions.question: Which mark correctly joins two independent clauses without a conjunction?
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses; a comma alone would create a comma splice.

lessons.title: 🧪 Full SAT Mock Test 2
lessons.html:
Module 13: Practice & AssessmentsAssessment

Full SAT Mock Test 2

Complete this full-length mock test under timed conditions, then review every answer explanation to close your gaps.

questions.question: A hypothesis says shade increases seedling survival. Which finding best supports it?
options: More seedlings were planted in shade
Survival was higher among shaded than unshaded seedlings
questions.explanation: The evidence must test the hypothesis's specific prediction about survival, not a related but different outcome.

questions.question: A passage opens with falling fish stocks and closes with a proposed quota system. Its structure is:
questions.explanation: The passage moves from stating a problem to proposing a remedy, the classic problem/solution arrangement.

questions.question: Goal: emphasise how quickly flooding spread. Which choice meets it?
options: The water rose across four districts within six hours.
Flooding is a recurring regional problem.
Residents described the flooding as severe.
questions.explanation: Only this choice conveys speed, which is the goal the question actually states.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct parallel structure?
options: She enjoys reading, to write and swimming.
She enjoys reading, writing and to swim.
She enjoys reading, writing and swimming.
She enjoys to read, writing and swimming.
questions.explanation: All three list items must share the same form; here all are -ing forms.

questions.question: Simplify (2³)² ÷ 2⁴.
questions.explanation: Power of a power multiplies exponents to give 2⁶, then dividing subtracts: 2² = 4.

questions.question: A plan costs $15 plus $0.10 per minute. In y = 0.10x + 15, what does 15 represent?
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is the value when x = 0, which here is the fixed charge before any minutes.

questions.question: Solve √(2x + 3) − 1 = 4.
questions.explanation: Isolating the radical gives √(2x + 3) = 5, so 2x + 3 = 25 and x = 11.

questions.question: Of 40 students, 25 are female and 10 of those study science. P(studies science given female) is:
questions.explanation: The condition 'given female' restricts the denominator to the 25 female students.

questions.question: The distance between (1, 2) and (4, 6) is:
questions.explanation: The differences are 3 and 4, giving √(9 + 16) = 5, a 3-4-5 triple.

questions.question: A student solves a percent question but reports the new price when the increase was asked. This is:
questions.explanation: The method was right; the mark was lost by not checking what the question actually asked for.

questions.question: What should you do before designing a study plan?
options: Take a diagnostic test to find your weaker section
questions.explanation: A diagnostic shows your starting score and which section costs you most, so study time goes where it pays.

questions.question: 'Yields rose in the north. ___, they fell sharply in the south.' Which transition fits?
questions.explanation: The two sentences contrast, so a contrast transition such as 'However' is required.

questions.question: A passage argues yields can rise, then says 'Admittedly, three seasons is a short record.' This sentence:
options: Acknowledges a limitation of the evidence
questions.explanation: 'Admittedly' signals a concession, which acknowledges a weakness without abandoning the argument.

questions.question: 'Schools with libraries score higher, so building libraries will raise scores.' The assumption is that:
options: The library, rather than something else, causes the higher scores
questions.explanation: The argument depends on the library being the cause rather than a marker of better funding overall.

questions.question: Which error type is unique to Expression of Ideas questions?
options: Choosing a fluent option that misses the stated goal
questions.explanation: Goal-directed revision questions punish choosing on style rather than on the purpose named in the stem.

lessons.title: 🧪 Full SAT Mock Test 3
lessons.html:
Module 13: Practice & AssessmentsAssessment

Full SAT Mock Test 3

Complete this full-length mock test under timed conditions, then review every answer explanation to close your gaps.

questions.question: 'The farmers who attended the training ___ reported higher yields.' What belongs in the blank?
questions.explanation: The relative clause is essential and no rule requires a mark; a comma would separate subject from verb.

questions.question: Simplify √48.
Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: The expression factors as (x − 2)(x − 3), so the solutions are 2 and 3.

questions.question: Factor x² − 16.
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares, which factors as (x − 4)(x + 4).

questions.question: A bar chart's vertical axis starts at 95, making a bar of 96 look much taller. This is:
options: A scale artefact; the real difference is about 1%
questions.explanation: A truncated axis exaggerates small differences visually without changing the underlying values.

questions.question: If every dimension of a cube is doubled, its volume becomes:
questions.explanation: Volume scales with the cube of the length factor, so doubling gives 2³ = 8 times.

questions.question: What reduces test anxiety most effectively?
options: Full-length practice under realistic timed conditions
questions.explanation: Familiarity with the real format and timing removes the surprise that drives most test anxiety.

questions.question: Where should you register for the SAT?
options: At the test centre on the day
questions.explanation: Registration is done through your own College Board account, where you choose a date, centre and upload a photo.

questions.question: In 'Unlike her ebullient brother, Sarah was reserved and quiet', 'ebullient' most nearly means:
questions.explanation: 'Unlike' signals contrast with 'reserved and quiet', so 'ebullient' must mean lively or enthusiastic.

questions.question: What is the recommended pace for a Reading & Writing question?
questions.explanation: With 27 questions in 32 minutes, roughly 70 seconds per question keeps you on pace.

questions.question: Which habit fixes both tone and purpose errors?
options: Checking the modifiers and evaluative language before choosing
questions.explanation: Adjectives, adverbs and prescriptive wording signal both the author's attitude and their purpose.

questions.question: When two options are both grammatically correct, the SAT prefers:
questions.explanation: Concision is an explicit SAT preference, so the shorter correct version is generally the answer.

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly capitalised?
options: She studied biology and English in Monrovia.
She studied Biology and English in monrovia.
She Studied biology and english in Monrovia.
She studied Biology and english in Monrovia.
questions.explanation: Languages are capitalised, other academic subjects are not, and place names always are.

questions.question: Express (3 × 10⁴)(4 × 10³) in scientific notation.
questions.explanation: Multiplying gives 12 × 10⁷, which renormalises to 1.2 × 10⁸.

questions.question: Simplify (3x² + 2x) − (x² − 4x).
questions.explanation: The minus distributes across both terms: 3x² − x² = 2x², and 2x + 4x = 6x.

lessons.html:

Full SAT Mock Test 4

Complete this full-length mock test under timed conditions, then review every answer explanation to close your gaps.

questions.question: A plot has perimeter 40 m and area 96 m². Its dimensions are:
questions.explanation: With w(20 − w) = 96, the solutions 8 and 12 give a rectangle of 8 m by 12 m.

questions.question: Of 120 respondents, 70 are rural and 42 of those own a phone. What percentage of rural respondents own a phone?
questions.explanation: The question restricts to rural respondents, so the denominator is 70: 42/70 = 60%.

questions.question: In a right triangle, the opposite side is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5. What is tan θ?
questions.explanation: The adjacent side is 4 by the 3-4-5 triple, so tan θ = opposite/adjacent = 3/4.

questions.question: When should Bluebook exam setup be completed?
options: On the morning of the test
questions.explanation: Completing setup in advance means download or device problems surface while there is still time to fix them.

questions.question: What identity document should an international candidate bring?
questions.explanation: International SAT candidates must present a valid passport matching their registration.

questions.question: How long is a typical Digital SAT Reading & Writing passage?
questions.explanation: Digital SAT passages are short, roughly 25 to 150 words, each paired with a single question.

questions.question: What should you do before reading the answer choices?
options: Summarise the passage in one sentence of your own
questions.explanation: Your own one-sentence summary gives you a standard against which to test each choice.

questions.question: What is the first step on a vocabulary-in-context question?
options: Predict your own word for the blank
Look up the root of the word
questions.explanation: Predicting first gives you a standard to match, which prevents the familiar meaning from misleading you.

questions.question: What does a topic sentence do?
options: States the single idea the paragraph develops
questions.explanation: The topic sentence names the paragraph's one idea, which every other sentence must serve.

questions.question: 'The new policy will ___ yields, and its ___ will be measured next season.'
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is the noun meaning result.

questions.question: Which calculator does Bluebook provide for the Math section?
options: A scientific calculator in module 2 only
questions.explanation: Desmos is built into Bluebook and available for the entire Math section.

questions.question: 'Seven less than three times a number is 14.' Which equation is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Seven less than' subtracts 7 from the quantity, giving 3x − 7.

questions.question: Which form of a quadratic most directly reveals the x-intercepts?
questions.explanation: Factored form y = a(x − p)(x − q) shows the roots p and q directly.

questions.question: A best-fit line has slope 0.8. This means each one-unit increase in x predicts:
questions.explanation: The slope of a best-fit line is the predicted change in y for each one-unit increase in x.

questions.question: Vertical angles formed where two lines cross are:
questions.explanation: Opposite angles at an intersection are always equal.

lessons.html:
Module 13: Practice & AssessmentsAssessment

Final Assessment

This is the Final Assessment. Pass it to complete the course and unlock your TIH Certificate of Completion.

questions.question: What should you do when stuck on a question?
options: Keep working until you solve it
Flag it, move on, and return if time allows
questions.explanation: Every question scores the same, so reaching easier later questions is worth more than finishing a hard one.

questions.question: Which calculator is built into Bluebook for the Math section?
questions.explanation: Bluebook includes the Desmos graphing calculator, available for the whole Math section.

questions.question: What is an assumption in an argument?
options: The first sentence of the passage
Something that must be true for the evidence to support the claim
questions.explanation: An assumption is the unstated link that the argument depends on, which is why attacking it weakens the argument.

questions.question: What is the correct order of work on a supporting-detail question?
options: Read the choices, then find the claim
Find the claim, then hunt for evidence
Read the whole passage twice first
questions.explanation: Identifying exactly what must be supported tells you what to look for among the choices.

questions.question: Which language signals a persuasive purpose?
questions.explanation: Prescriptive and evaluative wording indicates the author is arguing for a position.

questions.question: Which is the most efficient way to answer a logical-flow question?
options: Read only the sentences immediately before and after the blank
questions.explanation: The neighbouring sentences define the gap the answer must bridge.

questions.question: 'The report was thorough, it covered every district.' This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses are joined by a comma alone, which requires a semicolon, period, or conjunction.

questions.question: Which formula is NOT provided on the Digital SAT reference sheet?
questions.explanation: Geometry formulas are provided; algebra formulas such as slope must be memorised.

questions.question: If an equation reduces to 0 = 5, it has:
questions.explanation: A false numerical statement means no value of the variable satisfies the equation.

questions.question: In y = a·bˣ, what does a represent?
questions.explanation: Setting x = 0 gives y = a, so a is the starting value.

questions.question: In the model C = 45t + 300, where C is cost in dollars and t is hours, the 45 represents:
options: The cost per hour of running
questions.explanation: The coefficient on the variable is the rate of change, here dollars per hour.

questions.question: In a 30-60-90 triangle, the sides are in the ratio:
questions.explanation: The sides opposite 30°, 60° and 90° are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

questions.question: If module 2 feels noticeably harder than module 1, this usually means:
options: You were routed to the harder module, which is a good sign
questions.explanation: A harder module 2 indicates strong module 1 performance and access to the upper score range.

questions.question: What happens if you answer a Digital SAT question wrongly?
questions.explanation: There is no penalty for wrong answers on the SAT, which is why you should never leave a question blank.

questions.question: In 'The team proposed a novel approach', what does 'novel' mean?
questions.explanation: Here 'novel' carries its academic meaning, new or original, rather than its common meaning of a book.

questions.question: How far from the stated text should a correct inference be?
options: As far as general knowledge allows
It need not relate to the text
questions.explanation: SAT inferences are always one supported step from the passage, never a chain of assumptions.

questions.question: Why are extreme tone words usually wrong?
options: They never appear in answer choices
questions.explanation: SAT passages are measured academic writing, so tone answers are correspondingly moderate.

questions.question: A combined-sentence choice that omits information from one of the originals is:
questions.explanation: The combination must preserve all the original information; concision never justifies losing content.

questions.question: With subjects joined by 'or', the verb agrees with:
questions.explanation: With 'or' and 'nor', the verb matches whichever subject is closer to it.

questions.question: What is 5 − (−3)?
questions.explanation: Subtracting a negative is equivalent to adding, so 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8.

lessons.title: 14.1 SAT Study Planner
lessons.html:
📖 SAT Study Planner
A written plan that survives a bad week is better than a perfect one that does not.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

study planner

A structured schedule connecting tasks, dates, and score goals.

milestone

A measurable point showing progress toward a goal.

study block

A defined period assigned to focused practice.

progress tracking

Regular recording of completed work and results.

Build the plan backwards from your test date. Reserve the final week for review and one taper, the fortnight before that for full mocks, and everything earlier for targeted practice on your weaker section.

Write it down and keep it visible. A plan held in your head quietly becomes “whatever I feel like studying tonight”, which is always the section you are already best at.

Key points

  • Work backwards from the test date, reserving the last week for review.
  • Give the weaker section roughly twice the time.
  • Schedule specific topics, not “do some Math”.
  • Build in two rest days a week — a plan you abandon is worthless.
  • Re-diagnose every fortnight and adjust the allocation.
  • Keep the plan and the error log in the same place.

Example

An eight-week plan: weeks 1–2 fundamentals in the weaker section, 3–5 topic drills across both, 6–7 timed modules, week 8 a final mock five days out then review only. Two rest days weekly throughout.

Why this matters

The plan is what converts a distant 1600-point scale into tonight's specific task, and the fortnightly re-diagnosis is what stops it drifting toward comfortable work.

lessons.title: 14.2 Formula Sheet
lessons.html:
📖 Formula Sheet
Memorise the short list the app does not give you.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

formula

A symbolic rule expressing a mathematical relationship.

substitution

Replacing variables with known values.

unit

A standard measure attached to a quantity.

reference sheet

An organized collection of formulas for review or permitted use.

Bluebook provides geometry formulas on screen. It does not provide algebra, statistics or rate formulas. That asymmetry decides what is worth memorising.

The list below is complete for the Digital SAT. It is short, and knowing it removes the temptation to spend revision time on formulas the app will hand you anyway.

Key points

  • Slope: m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁).
  • Quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a.
  • Distance: √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²); midpoint: averages of the coordinates.
  • Circle: (x−h)² + (y−k)² = r².
  • Percent change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100; mean = sum ÷ count.
  • Exponential model y = a·bx; compound interest A = P(1+r)t.

Example

Print this list, keep it with your error log, and read it before every practice session. Geometry areas and volumes are deliberately absent — the reference sheet supplies them during the test.

Why this matters

Memorising the provided formulas wastes revision time; memorising the unprovided ones prevents the specific stalls that cost marks under time pressure.

lessons.title: 14.3 Grammar Cheat Sheet
lessons.html:
📖 Grammar Cheat Sheet
Every convention the SAT tests, on one page.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

grammar convention

A standard rule governing sentence formation.

clause

A word group containing a subject and verb.

modifier

A word or phrase describing another element.

sentence boundary

Punctuation or conjunction separating complete clauses.

Standard English Conventions is drawn from a closed list. This page is that list, and it is worth reading before every practice session until the checks become automatic.

Work through an underlined portion by asking the questions in order: is it a clause boundary, an agreement, a pronoun, a modifier, a parallel list, or a word choice?

Key points

  • Clause boundaries: two independent clauses need a period, semicolon, or comma + FANBOYS.
  • Agreement: cross out phrases between subject and verb, then match.
  • Pronouns: number match, correct case, unambiguous reference.
  • Modifiers: an opening phrase describes the noun after the comma.
  • Parallelism: list items and paired constructions share one form.
  • Word choice: affect/effect, its/it's, fewer/less, then/than, plus idiomatic prepositions.

Example

The order matters. Checking clause boundaries first settles every punctuation question immediately; only if no boundary issue exists do you move on to agreement, pronouns and the rest.

Why this matters

Conventions is roughly a quarter of Reading & Writing and is the most rule-bound part of the entire test, which makes this the highest-return page in the course to revise.

lessons.title: 14.4 Vocabulary List (1,000+ Words)
lessons.html:
📖 Vocabulary List (1,000+ Words)
Learn academic words in sentences, and prioritise the ones that keep appearing.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

academic vocabulary

Formal words common in educational texts.

word family

Related words built from one root.

collocation

Words that naturally occur together.

spaced repetition

Review at increasing intervals to strengthen memory.

The Digital SAT tests high-utility academic vocabulary in context, not rare words in isolation. A long list is only useful if it is worked through in phrases and revisited.

Prioritise words carrying a clear positive or negative charge, and words with a common meaning plus a distinct academic one — those are the two families the test draws on most.

Key points

  • Learn every word inside an example sentence, never as a bare definition.
  • Prioritise words with a common and an academic meaning: novel, qualify, sustain, arbitrary.
  • Note each word's charge: undermine negative, bolster positive.
  • Twenty words a week, revisited, beats two hundred skimmed once.
  • Group by theme — research, argument, change, causation.
  • Reading serious journalism daily is the most efficient supplement.

Example

Arbitrary means based on choice rather than reason, and carries a negative charge. In “the boundary was arbitrary” the author is criticising it. Knowing the charge answers tone and purpose questions as well as vocabulary ones.

Why this matters

Because the test moved away from obscure words, vocabulary is now one of the most improvable areas — the words that appear are the ones academic writing uses constantly.

lessons.title: 14.5 Practice Worksheets
lessons.html:
📖 Practice Worksheets
Practice counts only when it is timed, marked and reviewed.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

worksheet

A structured set of exercises for practising selected skills.

worked solution

A step-by-step explanation of a correct method.

self-correction

Revision of one's own error using feedback.

mastery

Reliable understanding demonstrated across varied problems.

Untimed practice with the answers nearby measures what you can do with help, which is not what the test reports. Set a timer, work without checking, mark honestly, then review.

The review is where the score comes from. For every wrong answer, write the reason: wrong question answered, sign error, misread unit, too-narrow choice, ran out of time.

Key points

  • Time every set from the first attempt; the clock is part of the skill.
  • Do not check answers mid-set — it inflates the result and teaches nothing.
  • Mark honestly, including student-produced responses that were nearly right.
  • Record the reason for each error, not just the correct letter.
  • Redo missed questions a week later, not immediately.
  • Two carefully reviewed sets beat five rushed ones.

Example

A student scores 14/20, and reviewing shows four errors were sign slips in distributing a minus. That is one habit, not four topics — and it takes an evening to fix rather than a fortnight.

Why this matters

Reviewed practice is the only kind that raises a score. Unreviewed practice mostly rehearses the errors you already make.

lessons.title: 14.6 Score Improvement Guide
lessons.html:
📖 Score Improvement Guide
Lift the weakest section first; the total is an average.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

score improvement

Measurable growth in assessment performance.

baseline

A starting result used for comparison.

priority skill

A weakness selected for focused improvement.

retest

A later assessment used to measure learning.

Because the total is the sum of two section scores, the fastest route upward is almost always the weaker section. Moving a 480 to 560 is far easier than moving a 690 to 720.

Within a section, target by question type rather than by topic. An error log grouped by reason usually shows two or three recurring habits accounting for most lost marks.

Key points

  • Work on the weaker section first — the total is a sum, not a maximum.
  • Target the question types costing you most, not topics you dislike.
  • Low scores usually improve through fundamentals; high scores through pacing and precision.
  • Grammar and conventions are the fastest points in Reading & Writing.
  • Linear equations and percentages are the fastest points in Math.
  • Re-diagnose fortnightly; without measurement you are guessing.

Example

A student at 520 Reading & Writing and 610 Math spends six weeks on Math because he enjoys it, and gains 20 points. The same six weeks on conventions and vocabulary in context would have been worth considerably more.

Why this matters

Score improvement is an allocation problem before it is a study problem. Deciding where the effort goes matters more than how many hours it is.

lessons.title: 14.7 College Admission Tips
lessons.html:
📖 College Admission Tips
The score is one part of an application, and rarely the deciding part.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

admission policy

An institution's current rules for evaluating applicants.

application deadline

The final date for submitting required materials.

transcript

An official record of courses and grades.

holistic review

Evaluation using multiple parts of an application.

Colleges read transcripts, essays, recommendations and activities alongside the SAT. A strong score opens doors; it does not by itself win a place, and a middling score is often offset by a strong record elsewhere.

For international applicants, check each institution's requirements individually: some are test-optional, some require the SAT, and several use score bands for merit scholarships even when admission is test-optional.

Key points

  • Check each college's requirement individually and in writing.
  • Test-optional for admission does not always mean test-optional for scholarships.
  • Aim for the middle 50% range published by each college.
  • Scores are generally valid for five years.
  • Score Choice lets you decide which sitting to send, where a college permits it.
  • Deadlines for scores differ from application deadlines — check both.

Example

A student is admitted test-optional but discovers the merit scholarship required a score by an earlier deadline. The place was never in doubt; the funding was, and it was decided by a date she had not checked.

Why this matters

Understanding where the SAT sits in the wider application prevents both over-investing in a score that will not move the decision and under-investing in one that funds the whole plan.

lessons.title: 14.8 Certificate Requirements
lessons.html:
📖 Certificate Requirements
What you must complete to earn your TIH Certificate of Completion.

Key Words & Meanings

Tap a word to open its definition.

certificate

A document confirming completion of defined requirements.

completion requirement

A task or standard that must be satisfied.

final assessment

The concluding evaluation of course learning.

verification

Confirmation that records and achievements are accurate.

The certificate records that you worked through the whole course, not that you achieved a particular SAT score. It unlocks automatically in the player once every requirement is met.

Lessons unlock in order, so the requirements are met by working through the course as designed rather than by seeking anything out separately.

Key points

  • Complete all core lessons in Modules 1–12.
  • Attempt every module quiz and section mock test.
  • Complete the Midterm Examination in Module 13.
  • Complete at least two Full SAT Mock Tests.
  • Pass the Final Assessment with 70% or higher.
  • Retakes are unlimited, so a failed attempt costs nothing but time.

Example

Once the Final Assessment is passed, the Certificate of Completion appears in the course player automatically. There is nothing to request and no waiting period.

Why this matters

The certificate documents completed preparation, which is useful evidence for a school, a sponsor or a scholarship application alongside the official College Board score report.
